newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-FREEMAN DELIGHTED WITH TITLE BUT DISPLEASED WITH RACE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-FREEMAN DELIGHTED WITH TITLE BUT DISPLEASED WITH RACE.

text.p: Cathy Freeman, unhappy with her technique in Monday's world 400 metres final, did not realise at first she had won.
"Technically, my race wasn't great and I was not quite sure I was first," the Australian confessed on Tuesday.
Still wearing her gold medal, the first Aboriginal to win a world title added: "I saw a friend of mine go crazy, then my name on the board and I thought 'well, I must have won'."
Freeman then embarked on a victory lap with both the Australian and the Aboriginal flags flowing from her arms.
"It was a way of saying that I'm proud of who I am and where I come from," she said. "I'm pretty proud of myself."
Freeman, who took two months off last year to visit schools in Australia, said she was planning to do so again, this time to meet children in the Australian bush.
"I'd like to go the bush," she said. "They (the Aborigines) have never had a world champion. Perhaps the kids would like to see me."

Asked what she would tell them, she said: "Of course, I'll say the things about commitment and perseverance and all that. But the most important message is that it doesn't hurt to love yourself. You must believe in yourself and never underestimate your strength."
Freeman, already looking forward to performing before her homes fans at the 2000 Sydney Olympics, pledged to remain unchanged by her victory.
"I'll stay the same," she said. "I'm blessed with the personality that I have but I'm nothing special. I'm just somebody who can run fast and deal with pressure."
